children: New Delhi, Nov. 6 -- Your friend asks you to stand as a guarantor for their loan and saying yes may seem like a simple way to help them. But, one must understand that the decision comes with financial and legal responsibilities that can outlast the friendship.

A loan guarantor is an individual who agrees to repay the debt if the borrower fails to do so at the time. Banks may ask for one when the borrower does not meet their income or credit score requirements, or when the loan amount is substantial or the repayment period is long.

However, becoming a guarantor is not just a formality. You sign a legally binding agreement, known as a guarantee, which outlines your obligation to repay the borrower's loan in case they end up defaulting.

Under Section 128 of the Indian Contract Act, the guarantor is liable to cover the debt, including any accrued interest and penalties. So, before agreeing to help a friend, understand the risks and when it may be wiser to say no.

In a blog post, published in August 2025, HDFC Bank has flagged some risks that potential guarantors should consider before entering into a loan guarantee agreement. Here are four key risks to assess before agreeing:

Before you commit to your friend about becoming their loan guarantor, it's a prudent approach to first check the said friend's financial stability and repayment history. You can also ask the borrower for their credit report.

If possible, you can also consider having co-guarantor to share the responsibility, although this does not automatically limit your liability. If you spot any discrepancies in your friend's credit report or see a trend of them relying on credit for daily expenses, it's better to say no to the arrangement.
